content.comment_body: Can anyone assist? I have connected a [product_name] module to an HMI panel. I used [product_name] engineering software version [version_no] to configure the HMI panel. The hours counter set up in the [product_name] module works correctly on its local display, showing hours and minutes. Now, I want the HMI panel to show the same data, but it doesn't work. Can someone tell me the correct tag in the engineering software for the HMI panel?
Can you specify what is not working—does the HMI not display anything, or is the displayed format incorrect?

Hello again. On the HMI panel, the IO field labeled xxxx.OT adds minutes directly; for example, 1 hour (60 min) plus 30 min gives a result of 90, instead of showing it as 1:30. I hope someone can help.

When using the h:m format, the [product_name] module sends the total number of minutes to the HMI (for example, 1 hour 30 minutes is transmitted as 90 minutes; 5 hours 45 minutes would be 345). This behavior cannot be changed in the [product_name] module's program. I'm not sure if it can be adjusted on the HMI configuration side. Alternatively, you would need to create a custom operating hours counter using multiple counters in the [product_name] module and send hours and minutes separately.
It's a tough day and night; I've managed a similar solution in the [product_name] module. Thanks. Best regards, [user_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing issues with displaying an hours counter in h:m format on an HMI panel connected to a [product_name] module. The value provided by the [product_name] module is communicated as total minutes, which does not meet the desired display format (e.g., 1:30 appears as 90). This data format mismatch between source and display causes confusion and usability problems.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the HMI panel to present operating time clearly in hours and minutes (h:m), replicating what is shown on the [product_name] module’s own display.
